input: A shell-and-tube exchanger installed in a refinery preheat train was used to heat cooling water, and the exchanger was found to operate at a duty of 852 kW. The hot stream entered the exchanger at 150 °C and left at 110 °C, while the cooling water entered at 30 °C and left at 50 °C. Based on these terminal temperatures, the log-mean temperature difference was calculated to be 89.6 K, and the installed area of the exchanger was 83.8 m2, which together give an overall heat transfer coefficient of 113 W m-2 K-1. This coefficient represents the combined performance of the exchanger as installed, bringing together the resistances of the two fluid films and the tube wall into a single figure referred to the installed area, while the log-mean temperature difference represents the mean driving force for heat transfer along the length of the unit. It is worth noting that the fouling of the exchanger was assessed on the basis of a single 90-day run, and that no cleaning cycle has yet been completed, which means that there is currently no information available about how much of the coefficient might be recovered if the exchanger were to be cleaned. The figures quoted here are therefore the figures for the exchanger in its current, as-found condition, and they should be used on that basis until such time as a cleaning cycle has been completed and the unit has been tested again.
target: A shell-and-tube exchanger in a refinery preheat train heats cooling water at a duty of 852 kW. The hot stream enters at 150 °C and leaves at 110 °C; the cooling water enters at 30 °C and leaves at 50 °C. The log-mean temperature difference calculated from the four terminal temperatures is 89.6 K, and the installed area is 83.8 m2. The overall coefficient obtained from the duty, the area and the log-mean temperature difference is 113 W m-2 K-1. The log-mean temperature difference is the mean driving force for the exchanger: the terminal differences at the two ends differ, and the log-mean value is the constant difference that returns the stated duty when it is applied over the installed area. The overall coefficient gathers the resistances of the hot-side film, the tube wall and the cold-side film into one figure referred to the installed area, so the coefficient describes the exchanger as built and as run, not any single surface within it. The two results are consistent as stated: the duty is the product of the coefficient, the area and the log-mean temperature difference, and the reported figures satisfy that product within the precision at which they are reported. The duty is the heat the hot stream gives up across the exchanger, and the terminal temperatures fix both ends of the exchange: the approach at the cold end and the approach at the hot end stand behind the single mean figure that the log-mean value reports. Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run; no cleaning cycle has been completed, and the recovery of the coefficient after cleaning is not on record.
